column3: The Hebrew names a purpose without an explicit Yours; BSB adds Yours.
The Hebrew has no introductory You asked or possessive My before counsel; BSB supplies both.
The Hebrew has no introductory You said; BSB supplies it.
The Hebrew has a singular ear and eye; BSB has ears and eyes.
The Hebrew leaves the object of rejecting unspecified; BSB adds my words.
The Hebrew says spoken to Me; BSB says spoken about Me.
The Hebrew describes lifting his face and speaking to Me; BSB describes accepting his prayer and speaking about Me.
The Hebrew says the LORD lifted Job’s face; BSB says He accepted Job’s request.
The Hebrew names turning Job’s captivity and his prayer for his friend in the singular; BSB says restoring prosperity and praying for friends.
The Hebrew names a qesitah without specifying silver; BSB says a piece of silver.
The Hebrew names Job’s latter part and beginning without explicitly naming days; BSB adds days.
The Hebrew repeats name for each daughter; BSB omits the repeated noun.
The Hebrew explicitly says his sons and his sons’ sons, four generations; BSB says children and their children to the fourth generation.
The Hebrew says full of days; BSB says full of years.
